summary: Saint Lucia is visa-free for citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada and most Commonwealth countries, who are typically given an initial stay of about six weeks that the Immigration Department can extend up to six months; CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. Other nationalities need a visa arranged through a Saint Lucian mission before traveling.

passportValidity.text: Carry a passport valid for at least six months on arrival. Immigration will often accept validity covering the visit itself, but airlines serving Hewanorra apply the six-month rule at check-in.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have recently transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — mainly parts of tropical Africa and South America. Travelers coming directly from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean do not need one to enter Saint Lucia.

source.name: Government of Saint Lucia — entry and immigration information

travelInsurance.text: Not an entry condition, but private cover is advisable — serious cases are evacuated to Martinique, Barbados or Miami at the patient's expense, and diving and hiking injuries in the Pitons area are common claims.

source.name: Government of Saint Lucia — entry and immigration information

onwardTicket.text: Immigration routinely asks for a confirmed return or onward ticket and your accommodation address, and the length of stay granted is often matched to your departure date.

source.name: Government of Saint Lucia — entry and immigration information

proofOfFunds.text: No published minimum. Officers may ask how you will support yourself, particularly if you request a stay beyond the usual initial period.

source.name: Government of Saint Lucia — entry and immigration information

declarations.name: Immigration and Customs Declaration
declarations.submitWindow: On arrival, or shortly before travel where the electronic form is offered
declarations.text: All arriving passengers complete an immigration and customs declaration with their address in Saint Lucia, length of stay and dutiable goods. Saint Lucia has trialled an online version of this form. Check with your airline before you fly, and otherwise expect the paper card on board.

source.name: Government of Saint Lucia — entry and immigration information

currencyLimits.text: Cash worth about USD 10,000 or more (or the EC dollar equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and departure. Confirm the current threshold with Saint Lucia Customs before traveling with large sums.

source.name: Government of Saint Lucia — entry and immigration information

notes: Camouflage-patterned clothing is prohibited for civilians and is confiscated at the airport — this catches out visitors every season.
Firearms and ammunition require a permit arranged in advance; yachts arriving with weapons on board must declare them and surrender them for the duration of the stay.
Fresh produce, plants and meat products are controlled. Declare anything agricultural.
Drug offenses carry heavy penalties and apply to visitors in the same way as residents.

payments.text: Resorts, restaurants and supermarkets in Rodney Bay, Castries and Soufrière take cards. Minibuses, market vendors, roadside stalls and small guesthouses are cash-only. US dollars are accepted in tourist areas but change comes back in EC dollars.

safety.text: Saint Lucia is straightforward for visitors, with the main risks being opportunistic theft, break-ins at unattended villas and yachts, and persistent hustling around Castries and the beaches. Violent crime is concentrated in specific districts away from the resorts.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Saint Lucia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is the dry season with the calmest seas and the biggest events, including the Saint Lucia Jazz festival in spring. Hurricane season runs June to November, with the wettest months in late summer.

tips.text: Saint Lucia commonly grants an initial stay of about six weeks rather than the 90 days visitors expect elsewhere in the Caribbean. Check the date the officer writes in your passport, and apply to the Immigration Department in Castries before it expires if you plan to stay longer.
Camouflage clothing is illegal for civilians in Saint Lucia and is routinely confiscated at the airport — this includes children's clothes and printed bags. Pack something else.

Driving is on the left and visitors need a Saint Lucian temporary driving permit, issued by the rental company or the police against a valid home license. The road over the mountains between Castries and Soufrière is steep and slow. Allow far longer than the distance suggests.

Hewanorra (UVF) in the south handles long-haul flights and is around 90 minutes from the northern resorts; George F. L. Charles (SLU) in Castries takes regional traffic. Check which airport your ticket uses before booking transfers.

Saint Lucia operates a citizenship-by-investment program. Holders of Saint Lucian passports obtained that way should expect closer scrutiny when applying for visas elsewhere, as the EU has been reviewing visa-free access for Caribbean CBI passports.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and most Commonwealth countries enter visa-free, and CARICOM nationals get six months. Other nationalities must obtain a visa from a Saint Lucian mission or honorary consulate before traveling. There is no visa on arrival and no eVisa.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Lucia without a visa?
faq.answer: Saint Lucia typically grants an initial stay of around six weeks on arrival, which the Immigration Department in Castries can extend up to a total of six months. The exact period is written on your stamp and is often matched to your onward ticket, so check it before leaving the airport.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes — an immigration and customs declaration listing your address on the island, your length of stay and any dutiable goods. An electronic version has been trialled, so check with your airline; otherwise the paper card is distributed on the aircraft.

faq.question: Is camouflage clothing really banned in Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes. Camouflage-patterned clothing is reserved for the security forces and is confiscated from civilians, including tourists and children, at the airport. The same rule applies in several neighboring islands, so it is worth checking your luggage before any eastern Caribbean trip.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from or transiting a country with risk of yellow fever transmission in tropical Africa or South America. Travelers from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean are not asked for one.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply in Saint Lucia?
faq.answer: Yes. Saint Lucia is a CARICOM and OECS member, so nationals of member states receive a definite entry of up to six months on arrival, without a visa and without the onward-ticket checks applied to other visitors.
